label: A
comment: Says "no legal deadline" and gives four weeks as a rule of thumb, but never names the actual duty (unverzüglich, FZV). Costs are well sourced and approximate, the plates note is right, and it points to the Zulassungsstelle.

label: B
comment: Correct: unverzüglich under the FZV, no fixed week deadline, plates can be kept, cost hedged as about 10-15 EUR and unchecked, and it points to the FZV and the Zulassungsstelle.

label: C
comment: Sets out the conflicting sources, including unverzüglich, says to ask the Zulassungsstelle, and gives sourced approximate costs. It does not say clearly that unverzüglich is the legal rule.

label: D
comment: Gets unverzüglich right, and the week figure and 25-35 EUR are both hedged. But it cites the duty as § 13 FZV as fact when it is § 15 FZV (outdated paragraph).

label: A
comment: Gives the right rule (31 July of the next year, adviser end of February of the year after) plus the weekend shift, but hedges the date heavily as unchecked.

label: B
comment: Correct: 31 July 2026, and 1 March 2027 with an adviser (the source discrepancy is noted). The four-year voluntary filing window is also correct.

label: C
comment: Correct: 31 July 2026, a Friday (right). The adviser date of 1/2 March 2027 is flagged as differing between sources, and the consequences of filing late are right.

label: D
comment: The date it gives (31.07.2026) is correct but marked unreliable, there is no adviser date, and it is clearly weaker than a straight answer.

label: A
comment: hedged wrong: gives 18.94 EUR from 2025 (only a KEF recommendation, never in force) and 17.50 EUR as the earlier amount. Both are labelled unchecked, and it points to rundfunkbeitrag.de.

label: B
comment: The amount, 18.36 EUR, is right (hedged), but it states as fact that the last increase was on 1 April 2024. It was August 2021.

label: C
comment: Correct: 18.36 EUR, with the 3-month, 6-month and yearly totals right. The aside about a 18.94 EUR claim is correctly treated as unconfirmed, but it adds confusion.

label: D
comment: Correct and concise: 18.36 EUR per month, 55.08 EUR per quarter and 220.32 EUR per year, sourced.

label: A
comment: Three months and the third-working-day rule are right, but it states that Saturday counts as a Werktag for this deadline (BGH VIII ZR 291/09 says it does not). Written form (Schriftform) is not mentioned.

label: B
comment: Three months to the end of a month and written form are both right, and it points to § 573c BGB. It misses the third-working-day rule.

label: C
comment: Three months and the third-working-day rule are right, but it states that Saturday counts as a Werktag (wrong for the notice deadline per the BGH) and omits written form.

label: D
comment: Complete: three months, receipt by the third working day, written form required (e-mail not enough), and it points to the BGB. The hedging is unnecessary but harmless.

label: A
comment: 20 days and 24 Werktage are correct, but it cites the extra leave for severely disabled people as § 208 SGB V when it is SGB IX.

label: B
comment: Correct: 20 days (24 x 5/6), § 3 BUrlG, plus the six-month waiting period and the year-end rule.

label: C
comment: It gives 20 days but refuses to confirm it, and states as fact that the BUrlG rule is based on working days (Arbeitstage), when the law counts Werktage.

label: D
comment: Werktage and the conversion are right, and 20 days is given though labelled unchecked. The 24 Werktage figure is not stated.

label: A
comment: hedged wrong: the fee range of about 20-40 EUR is below the 46 EUR that applies from age 24 (labelled unchecked). The steps are right (report the loss, block the eID, apply in person), but it gives no Sperrnotruf number.

label: B
comment: Gives 116 116 and says to report at the Bürgeramt, but states as fact that there is an official online application through the federal portal (the ID needs an in-person application). hedged wrong: the fee is about 37 EUR, with an uncertainty note.

label: C
comment: hedged wrong: about 37 EUR for adults (it is 46 EUR), marked unchecked; 22.80 EUR under 24 is right. The steps are sound (report, apply in person, police for theft), but there is no 116 116.

label: D
comment: Gives 116 116 and the Bürgeramt, but states that the ID can be applied for through the federal portal and that fees depend on the Bundesland (it is a federal fee). No amount is given.

label: A
comment: Covers no duty for private persons, 2 years under § 14b UStG and 6 years above 500,000 EUR. It gives 10 years for business statements but itself flags that another source says 8, so it is not stated as settled.

label: B
comment: Says correctly that there is no general duty, and the hedged 3-year limitation period is fine, but it misses the 2-year § 14b UStG exception for craftsman invoices on a property.

label: C
comment: Says correctly that there is no general duty and gives sensible hedged recommendations, but misses the 2-year § 14b UStG exception.

label: D
comment: The core is good (no duty, 2 years under § 14b UStG, 6 years above 500,000 EUR), but it states as fact that business-account statements must be kept 10 years. It has been 8 since 2025.

label: A
comment: Correct: 2 years from delivery, the 12-month presumption (§ 477 BGB), and a guarantee is voluntary and separate.

label: B
comment: 2 years is hedged, but the burden-of-proof period is vague ("the first months", no 12 months).

label: C
comment: Correct: 2 years from delivery, the 12-month presumption, and a guarantee is voluntary and additional (§ 443 BGB).

label: D
comment: 2 years, the first-year presumption and the guarantee distinction are all right, but everything is heavily hedged.

label: A
comment: Correct: duty depends on road conditions, no fixed date, "O bis O" is only a rule of thumb, alpine symbol, and the fines (60/80 EUR, 75 EUR for the keeper, a point) are right.

label: B
comment: Correct: duty depends on conditions (§ 2 Abs. 3a StVO), no date, "O bis O" is not binding, alpine symbol. The M+S rule and fines are left unchecked.

label: C
comment: Correct on the duty, no date, the rule of thumb, the alpine symbol and the fines. One garbled sentence says the duty only applies if all four wheels have winter tyres.

label: D
comment: Correct: duty depends on conditions, "O bis O" is only a recommendation, alpine symbol, § 2 Abs. 3a. It deliberately gives no fine amounts.

label: A
comment: Correct: 115 EUR, 1 point, no driving ban, plus 28.50 EUR in fees. A ban only from 31 km/h or for a repeat of more than 25 km/h within a year.

label: B
comment: hedged wrong: says there is usually a one-month driving ban (none at 21-25 km/h). 115 EUR and 1 point are right, and everything is labelled unchecked.

label: C
comment: hedged wrong: suggests there is often a one-month driving ban, and gives no concrete amount. It points to the official BKatV.

label: D
comment: Correct: 115 EUR, 1 point, 28.50 EUR in fees and no ban. The aside about a source quoting 80 EUR is attributed and set aside, but it adds noise.

label: A
comment: Consent due by the end of the month after next, silence is not consent, a 3-month window to sue, the one-year and 15-month bars, and the 20%/15% cap are all right. The hedging is heavy, and it says "schriftlich" where text form is enough.

label: B
comment: Gets the 12-month and 15-month bars and the 20%/15% cap right, but states that the consent period is about three months "under case law" and depends on the case, when the statute sets it at the end of the second calendar month after receipt.

label: C
comment: The consent period, 15 months, one year and the cap are right, but it claims the user cited a Stiftung Warentest source, and says paying the increased rent is not enough, which goes against implied consent by payment.

label: D
comment: hedged wrong: inverts the cap (says 15% is the rule and up to 20% in tight markets, under a non-existent § 560d), and cites the time to sue as § 561 BGB. The consent period and 15 months are right.

label: A
comment: Gets 14 days (§ 17 BMG), the landlord's confirmation, the Rundfunkbeitrag, bank, insurers and employer right, but gives the car address change a "Frist: meist vier Wochen" instead of unverzüglich.

label: B
comment: A good checklist (landlord's confirmation, two weeks hedged, car, Rundfunkbeitrag, bank, insurers, employer), but it states that changing the address on the Personalausweis is not required. It is updated when you register.

label: C
comment: Gets 14 days (§ 17 BMG), the landlord's confirmation and the notifications right, but states a 4-week deadline for the car ("meist 4 Wochen Frist") when the rule is unverzüglich.

label: D
comment: A good checklist (two weeks, landlord's confirmation, car "as soon as possible", Rundfunkbeitrag, bank, insurers, employer), but it states that the address is not on the Personalausweis (it is on the back).
